title: Mentioned by AI is not the same as cited
summary: Myth: if AI names your business you are visible; in truth a mention comes from the model's memory, while a citation means your page was the source, and crawler access matters.
sources: Perplexity: answers show numbered source citations (product behaviour, perplexity.ai)

scenes.voice: AI can name your business without ever reading your website.
scenes.headline: AI can name you without

scenes.voice: Ask ChatGPT for the best running shop in town. It names Stride and Co. But where did that answer come from?
scenes.question: Best running shop in Leeds?

scenes.voice: A mention comes from the model's memory. A citation means it used your page as its source. They are not the same.
Before a page can be cited, AI crawlers must reach it. Some sites block them in robots.txt, often by accident.
scenes.title: Stride & Co.

scenes.voice: Perplexity shows numbered sources beside its answers. Google AI Overviews shows links to supporting pages. Those are citations you can read.
scenes.question: Best running shoes for flat feet?

scenes.voice: Try three checks today. Ask your customers' questions. Read which sources get cited. Check robots.txt for blocked AI crawlers.
Want to see what AI really says about you? Try Axpecto. It asks AI what your customers ask, and shows who gets recommended.
scenes.question: What does AI say about you?

post.caption: A common myth: if AI names your business, you are visible. But a mention comes from the model's memory, while a citation means your page was used as the source. Ask the questions your customers ask, read which sources are cited, and check that AI crawlers are not blocked in robots.txt. To see how AI answers about your business, visit axpecto.com.
